sections.heading: Neutral-point voltage oscillation
sections.text: If the split DC-bus capacitors oscillate (V_neutral drifts from V_dc/2), reduce the balancing loop gain or increase the DC-bus capacitance. If the oscillation frequency is near the current-loop bandwidth, the balancing and current loops are interacting — decouple them by reducing balancing bandwidth.

sections.heading: THD failure
sections.text: If output current THD fails spec, check: (1) LCL filter resonance is between 10*f_grid and fsw/2, (2) active damping is enabled (capacitor-current feedback), (3) dead-time compensation is applied. Dead-time distortion is worse at low modulation index.

sections.heading: Overshoot from voltage loop
sections.text: DC-bus overshoot under load step: the voltage loop is too slow or the anti-windup is not working. Reduce voltage-loop kp or add proper anti-windup on the current reference saturation. The three-level topology has more headroom than two-level but the voltage loop design is the same.

sections.heading: Slow settling
sections.text: If the DC bus settles slowly after a load step, the voltage-loop bandwidth is too low. Increase kp/ki, but keep f_cv < fsw/100. If the current loop is also slow, the dq decoupling may be incorrect — verify the decoupling terms use the actual filter inductance.

sections.heading: Architecture limit
sections.text: If the NPC cannot meet THD or efficiency specs, consider: (1) higher switching frequency (at the cost of switching losses), (2) T-type for lower voltage (<600V DC bus), (3) cascaded H-bridge for higher voltage (>3kV).
